solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Would you mind the setter maybe using Latin?

definitions.text: Would you mind the setter maybe
definitions.meaning: surface reading: a polite query to the crossword compiler about the language used
setter's reading: a setter is a breed of dog, and 'mind' means watch out for, so this is a Latin warning sign about a dog

explanation.walkthrough: The setter here is not the compiler but the gun dog of that name; the Latin phrase was written at Roman doorways, as at Pompeii.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase translates as 'beware of the dog', a warning to mind any hound, setters included.

clue.text: Reporting by journalists of cause of sailing incident in bay?

parts.note: a cove is a small bay
on the model of road rage, the anger behind a nautical clash in a cove

explanation.surface: Press reports on what caused a boating mishap in a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Road rage causes road incidents; the clue imagines its waterborne cousin in a cove, so the bay comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the amount and manner of reporting a news story receives from the press.

clue.text: Film made with fourth edition of dictionary coming up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom of the light upwards

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
the fourth edition is numbered in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A film produced using a new edition of a dictionary that is about to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film, as a verb or noun; here the noun for a recording.

clue.text: Winger is kid on edge

parts.note: to kid is to tease, as is to chaff
to edge forward is to inch along

explanation.surface: A wide footballer is a youngster who is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer and 'on edge' a nervous kid, but 'on' only places the teasing above the creeping in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaffinch is a common finch, and any bird is a winged creature, hence a whimsical winger.

clue.text: Jack has got everyone's deliveries wrong

parts.note: in cribbage, 'his nob' is the jack of the turned-up suit
everyone is all, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Jack has mixed up all the parcels he was meant to deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery by the bowler, for overstepping the crease or similar.
explanation.definitionFit: No-balls are cricket deliveries ruled illegal, so they are deliveries that went wrong.

clue.text: Old taxman visiting Amsterdam at the weekend

indicators.note: the answer is a guest staying briefly inside the words that follow

parts.note: sitting across the end of Amsterdam, the next two words and the start of weekend

explanation.surface: A retired tax collector spends his weekend in Amsterdam.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Matthew was a tax collector before following Jesus, so an old taxman indeed.

clue.text: Correct English book, appreciated all round

indicators.note: all round means one word wraps entirely around the others

parts.note: dug is slang for liked or appreciated
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A well-received English textbook is corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug is to correct errors, usually in computer code.

clue.text: Hang out tops to dry, with exotic lacy lingerie

indicators.note: tops are the uppermost parts, which in words are the opening letters

parts.words: to dry, with exotic lacy lingerie
parts.note: initials of dry, with, exotic, lacy, lingerie; 'to' is skipped as a link

explanation.surface: Peg out fancy lace underwear on the line to dry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang out' looks like an instruction about washing, but it is the definition, in its sense of living somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out somewhere informally means to live or spend time there, as does to dwell.

clue.text: Here on-line courses, Polish and so on, are cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so a final letter is lopped off

parts.note: to buff is to polish
et cetera, abbreviated
the word are, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: Internet courses on Polish and similar subjects are being cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' means on a railway line and courses are meal courses; 'Polish' is not the language.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is the railway carriage where food is served, a place for meals on the line.

clue.text: Country fellow with stories to tell

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk

explanation.surface: A country man with plenty of tales to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of sayings or anecdotes about a person, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a nation on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Backing an opponent of violence, mostly with King in spirit

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
backing means moving in reverse, so the letters are read right to left
in places one element inside the other

parts.note: the indefinite article
a dove, a peace-lover, with its last letter dropped
chess abbreviation

explanation.surface: Supporting a pacifist, with a king in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the general term for such liquors.

clue.text: Queen to take off in pursuit of rear admiral?

parts.note: a butt is the rear end
Elizabeth Regina
to take off is to fly

explanation.surface: The Queen is to set off chasing a rear admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear admiral' is a naval rank, but 'rear' belongs to the wordplay and 'admiral' alone is the definition; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral and white admiral are species of butterfly, so an admiral is one example.

clue.text: Lexicographer, originally from OU, dispatched entire contents of Chambers?

indicators.note: dispatched as in sent off and scattered, so the letters are sent into a new order
originally points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its initial letter
taken as written
taken as written; the Open University in the surface

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker from the Open University sent off the whole text of the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a famous dictionary, which suits the lexicographer, but here chambers means rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomful is as much as a room holds, the whole contents of a chamber.

clue.text: He painted large bat on house

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y means X is placed after Y, so the house piece goes in front

parts.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
in cricket, a side batting is said to be in, so to bat is to be in

explanation.surface: An artist painted a big bat on a house wall.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the house first, followed by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German-Swiss painter at Henry VIII's court.

clue.text: Twig I replanted to make things even

parts.note: to twig is to understand, to get it
the Roman numeral for one
sown back in, put into the ground again

explanation.surface: A twig that I planted again is meant to balance things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a sprig to replant, but it is a verb meaning understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To get one's own back is to take revenge, settling a score so both sides are level.

clue.text: Volatile situation in Brixton unfolding, journalist recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards
in places one element inside the other
unfolding suggests something opening out and changing its shape

parts.note: taken as written
an editor

explanation.surface: A reporter recalls a tense stand-off unfolding in Brixton, the London district known for its 1981 riots.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox is literally a box of kindling; figuratively, any situation that could flare up.

clue.text: Disapprove of having very brief word with Yankee? Tough!

indicators.note: having means holding something inside

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
very cut down to its abbreviation
a verb is a type of word
Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Frowning on a curt exchange with an American: hard luck!
explanation.walkthrough: A bovver boy is British slang for a skinhead hooligan looking for trouble (bovver = bother). 'Tough!' looks like an exclamation of sympathy but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a violent ruffian, which is just what a bovver boy is.

clue.text: Side with monarch and Scottish banker providing support

parts.note: the side of a coin bearing the monarch's head
a river is a banker since it has banks; the Tay is Scotland's longest

explanation.surface: Siding with the king and a Scottish bank manager who offer financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' in crosswords is often a river, and 'side with' is not a verb but a coin face.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstay is the rope or wire supporting a ship's mast from the bow.

clue.text: Historic work coming in awfully handy: not a poem

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: taken as written
a poem is a verse

explanation.surface: A history book arriving very conveniently, though it isn't poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a poem' reads as a denial, but 'not a' is fodder and the poem is added in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Adverse is Hervey Allen's 1933 historical novel set in the Napoleonic era.

clue.text: Harmful refusal by native Americans to swap tips

parts.note: a refusal

indicators.note: swapping the tips exchanges the first and last letters, rearranging the word

parts.note: the Sioux people of the Great Plains

explanation.surface: A damaging refusal by Native Americans to exchange advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' look like pieces of advice, but they are the ends of the tribe's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious means poisonous or injurious, so harmful.

clue.text: English castle with a Lord's single key

parts.note: taken as written
Lord's is the London cricket ground, where a single is one run
the Delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A castle with a nobleman's lone key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord's' looks like a peer's possessive; it is the home of cricket in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel Castle in West Sussex is the seat of the Dukes of Norfolk.

clue.text: Party chief's territory

parts.note: a do is a party
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: The area controlled by the leader of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a realm or area under someone's rule, a territory.

clue.text: Pressure unduly apparent — a mark of democracy?

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see
taken as written
a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Is a heavy tax burden the obvious sign of a democracy?
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax is to strain or burden someone beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Don to assess student teacher's finals with that

indicators.note: finals are the last parts, so the closing letters are wanted

parts.note: the final letters of student and teacher
yon is an old or dialect word for that

explanation.surface: A university don comes to evaluate a trainee teacher's last exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university tutor but is the verb meaning put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To try on a garment is to put it on to judge its fit, donning it to assess.

clue.text: Having finished twice, given a tip

parts.note: time's up means it has finished
a second word for finished

explanation.surface: Having completed something twice, someone was handed a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity, but it means tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upended has been turned upside down, tipped over.

clue.text: Ruin suit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to destroy or finish off
second meaning: to serve or be adequate for

explanation.walkthrough: Both are British informal phrasal-verb senses: 'that'll do for him' and 'that will do for me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to wreck or kill and to be good enough for someone.

clue.text: Record of Turkish governor visiting in foreign lands

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place

parts.note: overseas
a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor

explanation.surface: An account of an Ottoman official's travels overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like an account but means an LP: the Beatles' 1969 album.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbey Road is the Beatles album named after the street of their London studio.

clue.text: Are becoming bothered primarily by police's image

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter
an E-fit is a British police composite picture of a suspect

explanation.surface: People are growing worried, chiefly by the way the police look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' looks like 'turning into', but here it means suitable or flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be suitable for, which is what being becoming means.

clue.text: All off, presumably, to see old president

wordplay.note: if all is off, then nothing (nix) is on

explanation.surface: Everyone left, it seems, to visit a former US leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Nix is slang for nothing; 'presumably' warns of the loose leap from everything off to nothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th US President, resigning in 1974.

clue.text: Excursion with host to see body of church

parts.note: a sally is a trip or sortie
a host is a great multitude, especially an army

explanation.surface: A trip with the person hosting to view the nave of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sally Army is the British nickname for the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army is a Christian denomination and charity, a church organisation.
